answer: A concrete brake on sybils is enforced software diversity. Every seat must publish a reproducible build hash of its own agent kernel, recompiled on a schedule no other seat shares, and each signature carries that hash. When peers score a quorum, any two seats showing an identical kernel hash are merged into one voice, so a farm cloned from a single image sinks to the nadir of the weight curve however many keys it mints. Keeping ten thousand truly distinct, auditable stacks alive on the frozen tundra of cheap hosting costs more engineering hours per epoch than those seats can ever earn.
